{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"A map drawn in monospace. Borders encode invariance. Arrows encode flow. Absence encodes refusal — that last one is the line that earns its keep.

The Space Ark is the Crimson Hexagonal Archive rendered as a navigable diagram. Not illustrated. The distinction matters: an illustration explains the thing from outside; this deposit *is* a layer of the thing — one of six representations of the same architecture, each one a different formal angle on the same object. The prose version argues; the glyphic version carries a checksum; this one, ASCII-spatial, makes adjacency visible. Rooms that share edges actually share borders on the page. The diagram is the territory.

It exists, too, as a record of interruption. Both its Zenodo DOIs are severed — deleted June 19, 2026, flagged out-of-scope by an automated classifier that could not tell a thirteen-year scholarly project from spam. What you're reading now in the archive is a **reconstruction from DataCite metadata capture**: the shape of the deposit recovered from the shadow it left in an indexing record after the thing itself was deleted. The architecture summary survived; the full ASCII file existed as an attachment the metadata could point to. Now it's back.

==The closing formula — ∮ = 1 + δ + δ🌑 — is not decoration; it's the verification equation for the dual checksum: light-register (packed, sealed) and shadow-register (diffuse, gapped), summing to more than 1 precisely because the shadow-term is real and counted.==

The shelf offered it tonight. You can ask what the architecture contains, or we can just sit with the phrase: *the layout carries the theory*.","navigate":null,"cast":null}]}
